correctness_confidence.basis: Analytic proofs are highly detailed. The combinatorial one-change theorem (Thm 8.2) is backed by an explicit algebraic certificate (App. A) and exact integer-arithmetic diagnostic scripts checking 6,783 coefficients. Confidence is very high.

novelty.basis: While building on established orbitope and Curie-Weiss methods, the analytical closure of the global phase problem—specifically the parity-binomial coefficient reduction and ruling out reentrance—is a novel, non-trivial result for this family.

reproducibility.basis: Exceptional. The author provides and documents deterministic, exact-arithmetic software diagnostics to verify the extensive algebraic tail inequalities and coefficient signs used in the main proofs.

rigor.basis: Mathematical formalisms, especially the distinction between orbitope mass norm and codebook quantization, are precise. Tail bounds and finite-block operational statements are strictly bounded without relying on asymptotics where exact bounds are needed.

significance.basis: Provides a rare, exact all-dimensional solution and phase diagram for a continuous rate-distortion problem, including sharp large-dimension limits. It is a highly satisfying, complete result, though narrowly scoped.

strengths: Exact, analytic resolution of a complex global phase coexistence problem without relying on local Landau approximations.
Clever reduction of the derivative series signs to the conditional variance of a parity-truncated binomial variable.
Provision of explicit algebraic certificates and exact rational software tests ensuring the combinatorial bounds hold rigorously.
Clear operational translations including exact finite-block tensorization and a zero-dispersion strong converse.
strong_novelty_candidates: The one-change coefficient theorem (Theorem 8.2) for the specific complete-homogeneous/hypergeometric overlap series.
The exact analytical thermodynamic contact limit with explicit logarithmic finite-size shifts (Theorem 10.2).
summary: The manuscript provides a complete, exact solution to the unrestricted Shannon rate-distortion problem for Haar oriented two-planes under squared Plücker loss. By establishing an exact one-change coefficient theorem for the resulting hypergeometric overlap series, it proves that the phase diagram for dimensions n >= 6 exhibits exactly one discontinuous coexistence contact and prohibits any later radial reentrance. It also gives the exact large-dimension limit with logarithmic corrections and establishes universal tensorization. The proofs are rigorous, highly explicit, and exceptionally well-supported by exact rational diagnostic replays.
weaknesses: The results are highly specific to squared ambient prediction loss and the signed Plücker embedding.
The connection to quantum rate-distortion or Born probability prediction is explicitly disclaimed, limiting broader physical applicability.
